NB01.title: the Front Porch
NB01.text:
May 22 — EP 30 — solo, 7 days food, the old tent.

Up 4:10 in town. On the water 6:20. T 38, calm, mist lying
in the low bays. The Front Porch by 8. Site ***, the island
one with the sitting rock facing east. Nobody.

Tent up wrong the first time. It's been a while. Fixed it.
Tea, bannock, the last orange. COLO pair working the bay,
one BAEA on the dead pine across. wt cold yet, cold enough
to make you honest.

Stone on the stump at the landing. Dad's habit.

Bed 8:40 with light still in the sky. WTSP going till dark.

0 pty.

NB02.title: Lake Two and Three
NB02.text:
May 23. Up 4:50. T 41. Fog sitting on the water like it
pays rent. Waited it out. c. x3.

On at 8. P 27r, P 39r, P 30r, 1x all three. The knee says
thank you. Two, then Three. Site ** in the pines past the
narrows. Good pad, no view. Somebody built a wall of rocks
round the grate the size of a hot tub. Took it back down.
Packed out their foil.

NW 10 by four. Rain on the fly at 9, the soft kind. Lay
there and listened instead of sleeping. Worth it.

NB03.title: the Kitchen
NB03.text:
May 26. Four, P 22r to Hudson, P 91r into the Kitchen, the
91 wet at the bottom like always. S 10.

Site *** on the point, the old one with the sitting log.
Islands every way you look. Forty years and I still check
the map twice on this lake.

2 WE 18 and 19 off the reef at dusk, slow jig. Kept the
small one. Thanked him. Ate him.

0 pty, 3rd day.

NB04.title: the 140
NB04.text:
June 18 — EP 27 — solo, 5 days food.

SW 15 on Snowbank and building. Kept to the S shore and the
lee of the islands. P 140r to Disappointment, rocky in the
middle, a spring at the low end coming out of the moss cold
as March. 2x.

Two cups out of habit. Poured the second one in the lake.

[Still pour it out.]

NB05.title: Disappointment
NB05.text:
June 19. Disappointment. Site *** on the N shore. Named by
somebody in a bad mood, the lake. Not my mood.

Up 5:00. T 52. Calm. HETH in the spruce behind the tent
before light, then the WTSP, then everybody.

COLO pair with 2 chicks on the back. Nobody ever looks as
proud as a loon with two.

NP 30 rel. Looked at me like I owed him money.

Rest of the day on the rock. Read. Slept. Read.

NB06.title: Coffee Lake
NB06.text:
July 21 — EP 30 — solo, 9 days food, the old tent.

Long day in. The Kitchen by 4, too tired to fish it.

July 24. P 17r off the Kitchen, down the Kawishiwi, P 30r
into Coffee Lake. Site *** on the beach, same as always.

Coffee Lake. 1988, off the beach rock, 8 ft. June laughed
for a week.

Looked for it at noon with the sun high. Glare. Didn't see
it. Didn't try hard.

Swam. wt swimming, finally. Sand between my toes in the bag
all night. Worth it.

NB07.title: the boys
NB07.text:
Aug 8 — EP 38 — the boys.

Little Sag. Same as every year. Write it up next year.

NB08.title: the Vermilion carry
NB08.text:
Sept 13 — EP 1 — solo, 6 days food.

Big water day. Off at 7, S 5, across before it woke up.
P 156r onto Trout, wide and dry, somebody keeps it up. 1x.

[Spring under the birch roots at the top end. Still running.]

Trout flat as a plate by 10 and stood up by 1. Got off at
the second point and waited it out under a cedar with the
jays. Site *** on the E shore, sand, a good long look N.

NB09.title: the red-and-white
NB09.text:
Sept 15. WB morning, NW 20 g30. Read the oatmeal box twice.
Good box.

Calmer by 4. NP 38 off the weed bed in the S bay on the
red-and-white. Biggest in years. Rel. He went back slow,
like he was thinking it over.

Lost the red-and-white after supper, a short cast off the
site rock straight into the crack at the waterline. Couldn't
reach it. It's there if your arm is longer.

NB11.title: Nina Moose
NB11.text:
May 17 — EP 16 — solo, 6 days food.

The Moose River high and brown with the melt. Every carry
wet at both ends. Lost count of the beaver dams. Pulled over
four.

Nina Moose by 2. Site *** on the E shore. Stone on the stump.

Moose cow in the creek mouth at 7, water to her belly. Didn't
move for me. We both had places to be and neither went. Calf
behind her in the alders, all legs.

NB12.title: La Croix
NB12.text:
May 19. P 100r off the Nina Moose into Agnes, then the 25r
to La Croix for lunch. Big water, big sky. Paddled over to
the Canadian shore and ate my sandwich on their rock. Nobody
asked. Paddled back.

[The other side looks the same as this one. That's the trick
of it.]

Agnes for the night. Site *** on the W shore, sand and pine.
NW 5, then nothing. Stars down to the water.

NB13.title: Sand Point
NB13.text:
June 9 — EP 12 — solo, 6 days food.

Off the Crane landing at 5. A.'s porch light on when I
passed. She leaves it on. Didn't stop: she'd feed me till
noon. J.'s boat already gone from her dock.

Sand Point by 10, S 10, the long reach straight as a road.
Three houseboats at the narrows, a dog barking on each one.

Site *** on the point itself, rock and red pine, the kind of
site you can't improve. Tried. Couldn't.

NB14.title: the Beatty
NB14.text:
June 11. Loon. The Beatty, 41r, the old rail bed under the
grass where they used to run the boats across on a cart.
Somebody cut a date in the rock at the landing a long time
ago. 1928, or 1923. Rum or boredom. Both, likely.

Site *** at the E end. SMB on everything, small. Fun for an
hour. Then supper.

NB15.title: the 64
NB15.text:
July 19 — EP 43 — solo, 5 days food.

Little lakes all day, the kind with no names you'd remember
by Christmas. P 64r Little Trout to Rum, short and steep and
all roots. Sat down hard at the bottom with the canoe on.
Perkele. No harm. The canoe thought it was funny.

Site *** on Rum, one pad, one rock, the whole lake.

0 pty.

NB16.title: Little Sag
NB16.text:
Aug 8 — EP 38 — the boys.

Little Sag with the boys. Whiskey brought the good whiskey
and the bad jokes. Deacon's knee. Teach's stove. Sparky kept
us up with the radio. 473r both ways, cursed both ways.

Dry. Water a foot down at the landings. WE deep and sulking.
Teach got a LT 31 on my old spoon and has told us 40 times.

I cooked. Nobody else near the pan. That's the rule.

NB17.title: the rock
NB17.text:
Aug 14. Last night. Sat on the rock till the stars came out.
They left me be. They always do.

Out tomorrow. The knee's had enough of the 473 for one life.

[Last one with me in it.]

NB18.title: the 186
NB18.text:
Sept 10 — EP 54 — solo, 5 days food.

Sea Gull in a W wind, which is Sea Gull's favourite trick.
Island to island in the lee. The old burn coming back in
jack pine to my chest.

P 186r to Grandpa and back in the afternoon for the walk.
Rock and blueberries, open, good looks back over the big
water.

Site *** on a rock island in the S part. Pad in a crack
between two ledges, sheltered from everything but the view.

NB19.title: smoke
NB19.text:
Sept 12. Smoke from the west all day. Sky the colour of a
bad egg. Sun at noon you could look straight at.

Radio says the Pagami fire ran east today, a long way.

Ash on the water by evening, fine as pepper. Thought about
the fall. Nothing to do from here. Hung the pack and went to
bed early.

NB20.title: V.'s water
NB20.text:
Oct 12 — EP 33 — solo, 5 days food.

T 30. Frost on the hull. On at 7:30, the landing all mine.
V.'s water at noon, NW 15. Didn't stop.

[Pink tape on the old blaze at the crews' rock. Not ours.
Not the FS either.]

NB21.title: the far end after the fire
NB21.text:
Oct 14. The far end after the fire. Burned to the rock up
top. Smell of it in everything. Ash to the ankle in the low
places. COLO on the water anyway, like nothing happened.

Cellar fine. Didn't touch what's on top.

Site at the far end. No stars. Never stars for this one.

NB22.title: Four Towns
NB22.text:
May 26 — EP 22 — solo, 4 days food.

Mudro in the rain. The carries in here are short and mean.
The bog one is a bog. Snagged the little silver spinner in
the rocks at the landing, reaching for the canoe of all
things. Gave it to the rocks.

Four Towns by 3. Site *** at the S end, the big flat rock
where you can look up the whole lake to the N bay.

Wolf scat on the trail to the biffy. Grey and hairy. Somebody
ate a deer.

NB23.title: Bootleg
NB23.text:
June 23 — EP 9 — solo, 5 days food.

P 206r off the Sioux into Bootleg, mud from the first step.
The lake's got the right name for its history if the old men
are telling it straight. Site *** on the point. Nobody for
two days.

Found an old tin of bottles in the rocks at the beaver pond.
Prohibition, by the glass. Left it. Some other fool can have
the glory.

NB24.title: the Long Room
NB24.text:
July 17 — EP 55 — solo, 7 days food.

Through the Sag islands with the sheet on my knee the whole
way. Every island looks like the last one.

July 19. The Long Room. Site *** under the cliffs. Water so
clear you can count the stones at 15 ft. June's favourite.
She'd say it was too clear to trust, and she was right about
most things.

LT 26 on the first drift with the copper spoon, deep. Kept.
Supper and breakfast.

Took a picture of the cliffs for her. Habit.

NB25.title: without me
NB25.text:
Aug 8. Town. The boys went in at Sawbill this morning
without me. Sparky called from the landing to tell me what I
was missing. Told him: the 473. He said Deacon's already
complaining. Good.

NB26.title: lights
NB26.text:
Sept 27 — EP 22 — solo, 4 days food.

Four Towns again for the fall. Maples gone red on the
ridges, the rest still thinking about it. Same site, same
rock.

Sept 28. T 34. Clear and still, the kind of night the sky
sits right down on the water.

Lights over the N bay, low, steady, then gone.
?

[Again. Same bay. Put my lamp on it and it went out.
?]

NB27.title: the sill
NB27.text:
Oct 12 — EP 33 — solo, 5 days food.

V.'s water rough, W 15. Through it. The far end by 3.

New sill on the camp. Old rail does fine.

c. x2. Fish none. Didn't try.

NB28.title: Perent
NB28.text:
June 8 — EP 36 — solo, 5 days food.

Down the creek with the beaver, a hundred dams and two
carries a canoe long. Perent by noon. Big shallow lake, a
wind lake. SW 10.

Site *** on the N shore, sand, a long way to look.

WE 23 off the reef point at dusk, 6 ft, slow jig. Best fish
of the year and it's June. Took his picture before he went
back. He didn't care for it.

NB29.title: the Kek
NB29.text:
July 20 — EP 54 — solo, 9 days food.

Ogish by the 2nd night, the little carries at the ponds, the
4 and the 16, wet feet both.

July 23. The Kek. Calm. Water like glass by the N shore. Bit
of red and cream down in 12 ft, riveted. Old plane. Said a
word over it.

Tried for a picture. Glare. Maybe.

Site *** at the W end, the high one. Laker water. Didn't
fish. Didn't feel like it after.

NB30.title: the man on the 563
NB30.text:
Aug 13 — EP 19 — solo, 6 days food.

On at 3, which was foolish. P 563r. Hot. Deer flies the size
of sparrows. 2x, so call it 1,689r walked. Didn't do the sum
till the end, which was wise. Voi voi.

Man on the 563r going the other way at dusk, no pack. Said
"Evening."

Aug 15. Back over the 563r, 1x this time, out of food and
pride. Same man at dusk. Same word.

[O. Took me till the third time. He knew me the first.]

NB31.title: Two Stump
NB31.text:
Sept 17 — EP 31 — solo, 5 days food.

Off the dock at 7. P 139r to Clear, wet at both ends.

[Split cedar at the top end, where we used to hang the lunch
pack. Down now. The stump's there.]

Site *** on Clear. Small lake, big pines, quiet.

Sept 18. Two Stump. Passed the old drill road landing. Birch
thick as my wrist on it now. We cut that clearing in a week.

NB32.title: the roof
NB32.text:
Oct 12 — EP 33 — solo, 5 days food.

The far end. Bark on the camp roof, moss over the bark.

Jays found me before the pot was on. Fed them bannock.
They'll tell everybody.

NB33.title: H. and T.
NB33.text:
Nov 21. Town. Coffee with H. at the home. Told him about the
far end in the frost. He says I'm a fool to go alone in
October. Says it every year. He's right every year.

T. on the bench outside the Legion after. We nodded. Forty
years of nodding.

NB34.title: Kawishiwi landing, Polly
NB34.text:
May 24 — EP 37 — solo, 6 days food.

Kawishiwi landing at 6. lvl high, the landing rocks under to
the second step and the little beach gone altogether. Mine
the only car in the lot but a ranger truck.

May 26. P 19r into Polly, the trail half under water.

[The 19 floods in May. Keep left. There's a ledge under it.]

Site *** on the point. WTSP, HETH, a winter wren that wouldn't
quit. Bugs up. Bug jacket on for supper.

NB35.title: Mummo's
NB35.text:
June 7 — EP 25 — solo, 4 days food.

Up the Front Room in a S wind, Newfound, Sucker. P 122r over
Prairie, 1x, the rangers waving from their side like they do.
Then down the bay.

Mummo's. Lilacs out. The step's still there.

The party on the next point came over to ask what the bushes
were. Told them lilacs. They asked who planted them. Told
them a lady.

V. and I learned to swim off that rock. He was better at it.
They said he drowned.

NB36.title: Big Moose
NB36.text:
July 15 — EP 16 — solo, 5 days food.

The Moose River low and warm. P 61r into Big Moose. Site **
on the quiet shore, good pad, bad landing, nobody on the
whole lake.

July 16. Something big walked the ridge behind the site at 2.
Two legs by the sound. I've heard bears on two legs. Not like
that.
?
Then a knock. Wood on wood. Twice.

Slept in the canoe, off the point, tied to a snag. Old man's
foolishness. Slept fine.

NB37.title: the sled
NB37.text:
Aug 19 — EP 30 — solo, 6 days food.

Blueberries on every carry. Ate my lunch twice.

Aug 21. The Kitchen. The old sled's still on the lunch rock.
Somebody's gone to the trouble of not moving it. Ate my lunch
beside it. Ash runners, the iron straps rusted to lace. Some
trapper's winter.

2 WE off the island reef. Kept one.

NB38.title: Cherokee
NB38.text:
Sept 9 — EP 38 — solo, 6 days food.

Ada, Skoop, P 190r down to the creek and Cherokee, all roots
and wet rock. 2x. The knee filed a complaint.

Cherokee in the afternoon with the wind laid down. Big pretty
lake, islands. Site *** on the island off the N shore.

Moose antler on the trail to the biffy, a shed one, chewed by
mice. Left it for the mice.

NB39.title: WB on V.'s water
NB39.text:
Oct 12 — EP 33 — solo, 6 days food.

WB on V.'s water. NW 25 g35. Took the site under the cliff
and sat the day out. Didn't sleep much.

0 pty.

Oct 14. The far end. Fished the bay the boys swore off. Still
lousy. Good.

NB40.title: Horseshoe
NB40.text:
May 30 — EP 48 — solo, 6 days food.

Meeds, Caribou, P 25r into Horseshoe. A good shape for a
lake: every bay a lee.

Site *** inside the bend.

Moose bull in the reeds across at 8, velvet just starting.
He ate for an hour. I watched for an hour. Fair trade.

NB41.title: Gaskin
NB41.text:
June 1. P 97r to Gaskin, up and over and down. Site *** on
the S shore.

Hung the copper spoon on a rock off the site point at dusk.
Line broke. It's there in 4 ft if the sun's right. I'll see
it next time and not be able to reach it then either.

NB42.title: Winchell
NB42.text:
June 3. P 61r to Winchell. The cliffs in the evening, every
ledge with a cedar hanging on by its fingernails. Took a
picture. It never comes out. Took it anyway.

Site *** across from them. Sat up late for nothing but the
look of it.

NB43.title: paintings
NB43.text:
July 9 — EP 77 — day.

South Hegman, P 10r, North Hegman. Calm. The narrows.

Paintings. Kept going.

Lunch on the rock at the N end. Back at the lot by 3.

NB44.title: the wolves
NB44.text:
Aug 20 — EP 16 — solo, 6 days food.

Agnes by the 2nd day. Same site. Same sand.

Aug 22. Wolves at 11, NE, three or four. Then not. Then the
loons answered them, which I've never heard in fifty years of
listening.

Aug 23. Tracks on the beach in the morning, big ones and
little ones, all over my landing. Pups. Put the paddle down
by them for the size and took a picture.

NB45.title: Brule, the Cones, Juno
NB45.text:
Sept 15 — EP 41 — solo, 5 days food.

Brule in a NW 15, big and grey and all elbows. Island site
***, the one with the two pads and the steep landing.

Sept 16. The Cones, P 38r, P 24r, all three of them in fog
this morning and the same lake as far as the eye's concerned.

[Three Cones and one name. Count the carries, not the shores.]

Sept 17. P 58r to Juno for the afternoon. Lost the yellow jig
in the landing rocks. Fourth this year. Half my tackle box is
on the bottom up here, which is where it wanted to be.

Sept 18. Out. Sauna at home tonight if the knee gets me there.
Löyly. My brother and I used to run from Mummo's sauna into
the lake in March and lie about how cold it was.

NB46.title: the stove
NB46.text:
Oct 12 — EP 33 — solo, 5 days food.

V.'s water flat and grey. The far end by 2.

Stove in at the camp. The drum's sound, the bung rusted shut,
which is right for a stove. Pipe up under the cedar.

Warm night. First warm one there.

NB47.title: the east end, the line
NB47.text:
May 21 — EP 69 — solo, 6 days food.

Long drive, the whole Shore and up the hill. The east end's a
different country. Hardwoods, steep, Superior in the air.
Site *** on John, nobody.

P 59r to Little John at dusk for a look. Nobody's lake.

May 22. Down the Royal as far as the beaver let me, P 93r
round the worst of it. Lost the brown jig in the rocks at the
Royal landing. First of the year and it's May. Promising.

May 23. North Fowl. The line runs straight up the lake. Site
*** on our side, S shore.

[You can stand on the line here, a foot each side. Did, once.
Felt like nothing.]

NB48.title: Deacon
NB48.text:
June 18. Duluth. Deacon's funeral. The boys carried. Sparky
cried the hardest.

Teach read the 23rd and got through it. Sisu. Whiskey stood
at the back with his hat in his hands like he'd stolen it.

Drove home in the rain. c. x4, gas station coffee, every cup
worse than the last.

NB49.title: Duncan, the Stairway, Rose
NB49.text:
July 14 — EP 60 — solo, 5 days food.

Duncan off the road at 7. Up the ridge trail for the view and
a picture, the lake below with the morning on it.

The Stairway down to Rose. Steps all the way, the falls beside
it talking to themselves the whole way down. Lost the white
spinner in the rocks at the bottom by the falls, trying for a
smallie that wasn't there.

Rose. Big border lake. Ontario across the water close enough
to hear their loons. Site *** at the E end.

NB50.title: Sag
NB50.text:
Aug 23 — EP 55 — solo, 5 days food.

Sag in a W 20. Hid behind islands all morning and got where I
meant to be by noon, which is the most you can say for Sag.

Site *** on an island in the S part. Good kitchen rock.
Nobody.

[Sag's islands lie to you. Count them off the sheet, not the
eye.]

NB51.title: the river
NB51.text:
Sept 6 — EP 35 — solo, 7 days food.

Isabella. Site *** on the S shore, a ledge and a pine, the
sort you come back to.

Sept 7. Down the river. Rice beds, the carries short, the
current with me. Nobody all day. Moose sign at every landing.
Good country to be an old man in.

Sept 9. P 65r up to Quadga. Lost the little brass spoon on the
first cast at the site, snagged in the crack under the landing
rock. Tied on another. Caught nothing on that either.

Sept 11. Back up the river and out. 0 pty since the 7th. Five
days. The best kind.

NB52.title: the new sign
NB52.text:
Oct 11. Town. Gas, coffee, the paper. New sign at the junction,
lit up at night now. Drove round by the lake to miss it. Twice.

NB53.title: the 205
NB53.text:
Oct 12 — EP 33 — solo, 6 days food.

T 31. V.'s water flat by ten. P 205r, the little one after. 2x.
Knee.

NB54.title: the long way round
NB54.text:
Oct 13. Took the long way round to the flowage. Dam's up a
foot. Good. Keeps the traffic down.

NB55.title: the notch
NB55.text:
Oct 14. Trolled from the burnt point toward the notch, 3 pulls.
Nothing. Flowage end.

Out by dark. c. x2 at the landing in the truck with the heater
on.

NB56.title: November
NB56.text:
Nov 22. Town. Skim ice at the narrows by the 20th this year.
Out by the 10th from now on. Never the far end in November.

NB57.title: let it go
NB57.text:
March 9. Town. Coffee with H. Told him about the new sign. He
said, so what, Walt, let it go. Same thing he said forty years
ago. I let him beat me at cribbage for it.

NB58.title: the ring
NB58.text:
May 18. Town. Pie at the café before the put-in. Two old faces
at the window table I'd hoped not to see again this side of
the cemetery. One still wears the ring. Ate the pie. Paid at
the counter. Left the coffee.

NB59.title: new letterhead
NB59.text:
June 22. Town. New sign at the junction's got friends now.
Coffee and cookies in a tent in the lot, everybody's name on a
sticker. Saw the ring and Thursday at the coffee. Same men, new
letterhead.

Didn't take a sticker.

NB60.title: Gene's
NB60.text:
July 12 — EP 38 — solo, 7 days food.

The Frost River carries, six or seven, I lost count and the
knee didn't.

July 15. Gene's. Site ***, his rock, his pine. Left his paddle
where he'd want it, in the crotch of the pine above the
landing, blade up. Sat a while.

The fishing here was always his and never mine. Still isn't.

NB61.title: the 121
NB61.text:
Aug 17 — EP 30 — solo, 5 days food.

Little lakes south of Two. Short carries, nobody, the WE small
and willing.

Aug 18. P 214r, P 121r. Hot. Deer flies.

Dry bag in the rocks at the top of the 121. Old guide's habit.

NB62.title: the Grumman
NB62.text:
Sept 14 — EP 30 — solo, 4 days food.

Towed the old Grumman in behind. She follows like a dog that
doesn't want to go to the vet. Carried her over the little
ones and came back for mine.

Sept 15. Left the old Grumman upside down in the alders at the
north end of the 214. Some kid'll need it someday.

NB63.title: the pages
NB63.text:
Oct 12 — EP 33 — solo, 5 days food.

V.'s water, N 10, cold and clear. P 205r, the little one, 2x.
The knee voted no and lost.

Oct 13. Looked in on the cellar. Dry. Kept to the east bank,
the flowage's high. Left some pages at the camp.

NB64.title: the hospital
NB64.text:
Nov 14. Duluth. Sat an hour with Sparky's boy at the hospital.
Second time for him. Thirty years old and talking about the
Twins like it's August. Good kid.

Drove home. Thought about the land man, first time in years.
Dead eight years and I still check the mirror.

NB65.title: bunk 3
NB65.text:
May 20. The Front Room. Bunk 3 for the summer. M. says fix the
dock and the bunk's free. Fixed the dock. She says it's crooked.
It's level. The lake's crooked.

NB66.title: the back door
NB66.text:
June 2 — EP 30 — solo, 5 days food.

South by the little lakes, the 214, the 121, the 63, every one
of them alive with blackflies.

June 3. Spare paddle under the cedar at the 50 off the back
door. White stone on it.

NB67.title: green Kevlar
NB67.text:
June 4. Green Kevlar on the second lake out, 2 men, new paddles,
no rods. Waved. I waved. Nice day for it.

NB68.title: one dark
NB68.text:
July 26 — EP 30 — solo, 4 days food.

July 28. Back door to the Front Porch in one dark. 9 h. Knee
says never again. It'll do it again.

Put the little radio in the dry bag at the top of the 121 on
the way through, batteries taped in a sock. Rangers' channel.
Weather.

NB69.title: boots
NB69.text:
Aug 25. Truck at the put-in with the engine running when I came
off the water. Fella by it in boots clean as Sunday. Didn't pass
me. Was waiting. Asked how the fishing was. Told him lousy.

NB70.title: the wrong hill
NB70.text:
Sept 22 — EP 30 — solo, 4 days food.

Sept 23. Somebody's been digging on the back door, NE shore.
Wrong hill. Good.

Survey tape, a hole filled half back in, a shovel somebody
broke and left. Didn't land.

NB71.title: fourth time
NB71.text:
Sept 24. Green Kevlar again, 2 men, no rods. Fourth time since
June. They wave like they've practised it.

NB72.title: company
NB72.text:
Oct 12 — EP 33 — solo, 4 days food.

V.'s water. Green Kevlar sitting off the S end. Not fishing.

Oct 13. Didn't go on to the far end. Not with company on the
lake.

NB73.title: saw cut
NB73.text:
Oct 14. Saw cut on a jack pine at the back door landing. Clean.
Fresh. Nobody cuts with a saw up here without a reason.

Out early. Clean Boots's truck at the landing with nobody in it.
Engine warm. Put my hand on the hood to be sure.

NB74.title: Thursday
NB74.text:
Dec 6. Town. Thursday had lunch with the ring again. Same table.
Ate my soup at the counter where they could watch me eat it.
Took my time.

NB75.title: quarters
NB75.text:
May 13. The Front Room. Bunk 3 again. M. says the dock held the
winter, which is more than I can say. Paid her in quarters. She
counts them out in front of me to make me laugh. Works.

NB76.title: Sundays
NB76.text:
June 16. Sparky calls Sundays now. Never used to. Asks after the
knee and which week.

NB77.title: the good coffee
NB77.text:
July 2. Town. H. at the home. Doesn't know the month any more.
Knew me. Knew the far end. Asked was the fishing still lousy.
Told him yes. Left him the good coffee.

NB78.title: the test
NB78.text:
July 7. Told Whiskey the Kek and Sparky the river. Will see who's
on which.

NB79.title: the result
NB79.text: Aug 7. Green Kevlar on the river Tuesday. Nobody on the Kek.

NB80.title: Teach
NB80.text:
Aug 15. Sawbill, the 15th. Thermos, bars. Shook every hand.
Told Teach one thing. He didn't ask which. Good man. Always was.

NB81.title: the fold
NB81.text:
Aug 21. Someone was through my pack at the bunkhouse. Folded it
back better than I do. That's how I knew. Book was on me.

NB82.title: the paper
NB82.text:
Sept 10. Town. Post office. One stamp. Girl asked was that all.
Said that was all.

NB83.title: fifteen foot
NB83.text:
Sept 28. Old 15 ft aluminium off a fella on the Range. Leaks at
the stern rivet. Put her in the alders on Birch with a tarp over.
Somebody'll need her.

NB84.title: the door
NB84.text: Oct 12. Paddled to the door and back. 4 h. In the dark, 5.

NB85.title: check-in
NB85.text:
Oct 14. The Front Room. Bunk 3. T 41. M. gave me the one by the
stove without asking. Dock's fine.

NB86.title: Clean Boots
NB86.text:
Oct 15. Clean Boots at the counter asking M. for a bunk he doesn't
need.

NB87.title: wind
NB87.text:
Oct 16.
6:00   SSE 10
12:00  SSE 10
18:00  SSE 15 g20
Radio says it holds to Fri.
Good wind for the other side.

NB88.title: the last page
NB88.text:
Oct 17. Bunkhouse. T 44. SSE 10.
Phone at 6. Asked was I in all week. Said yes.
Truck in the lot, lights off. 11:40. Still there.
Pack stays. Tent stays.
Out the door before they
Not the cellar. Don't go near the
If you are reading this

TP1.title: torn page 1
TP1.text:
Sept 24 1977. Saturday.

Rain from first light. We came up from the pond with a can each,
the tar on them still soft, and the old pit on the ridge the way
we left it last summer, the moss grown over the boards. V. dug.
By the time he had the new boards in and the moss back over them
it was near dark under the rain, and I held the light.

He said it smelled like the potato hole at Mummo's. The cellar,
he called it, and laughed, and that was its name.

He put a note on top for me and wouldn't let me read it. For
Saturday, he said.

He said we'd be back for them Saturday.

TP2.title: torn page 2
TP2.text: Where V. dug, the way the sun comes up at Christmas. Under the moss.

TP3.title: torn page 3
TP3.text:
Oct 12.

If it comes to it, the papers go to a newspaper. Not the sheriff.
Not the company. Not to A., she's had enough.

L1.title: Mummo's, drawn by a boy
L1.text: A child's map of a shore. A square with wavy lines on its roof labelled `SAUNA`. A long flat shape at the water labelled `THE ROCK`. A dock on legs, `DOCK`. Purple scribbles, `LILACS`. A stick figure in a long dress with a fish, `MUMMO`. A stump at the foot of the dock with a small white circle on it. An arrow off the edge of the paper: `PRAIRIE →`. In the corner, carefully: `BY WALTER H.`

L2.title: the burning
L2.text:
Feb 20 1965.

Burned Mummo's on the ice today. Dad lit it. Ma wouldn't watch.
Mummo sat in the truck with the heater and the window up.

Took the cookstove lids, the good chair, the coffee mill. Left the
step, we couldn't lift it. Left the lilacs.

A. cried. V. didn't, then he did. I held the dog.

Mummo says the lilacs will tell anybody who asks.

L3.title: the grub list
L3.text:
E-7. Aug. 12 days, 2 men. Plane Tues.

flour 10
lard 3
bacon 6
Spam 12
rice 5
oatmeal 4
sugar 4
powdered milk
tea
coffee 3 lb — the good kind (V.)
raisins, onions
smokes (V.)
.22 shells
cards

L4.title: a thank-you
L4.text: ⟩ Walt — Still telling everybody about that walleye. Wife says I've told it so many times it's grown two inches. Same time next year if you'll have us. Ray, Des Moines

L5.title: four from a church in Duluth
L5.text:
Aug 1985. Sawbill. 6 days. Four from a church in Duluth.

One brought a Bible and read it at the fire, and nobody minded.
One brought a bottle and everybody minded less.
One took my stove apart to see how it worked and put it back
better. One brought a radio.

Good men. Can't steer, any of them. Want to come back next year.
Told them fine, if they learn a J-stroke over the winter.

L6.title: June's bannock
L6.text:
Bannock

2 c flour
1 T baking powder
½ t salt
2 T lard
water till it's right

Fry slow. Walt, slow means slow.
— June

L7.title: for Walt, from Matt
L7.text: A canoe with four stick men in it and a fish bigger than the canoe, its teeth drawn in carefully. Across the top in capitals: `TO WALT`. Across the bottom: `THANK YOU FOR THE FISH STORY. FROM MATT. 4TH FLOOR.`

L8.title: while you were out
L8.text: ⟩ WHILE YOU WERE OUT — For: Walt — From: your sister — Time: 4:15 — Message: Nothing wrong. Call her back when you're in.

L9.title: coffee's on
L9.text:
W — coffee's on. Pour me one, back at 4.
— June

P1.text: Black and white, deckled edge. Two small boys in wet underwear on a long flat rock at the water, one standing (taller, Walt, 9), one sitting with his knees up (Eino, 6). Behind them a log sauna with a stovepipe, and a lilac bush taller than the sauna.

P2.text: Colour Polaroid, faded toward green. Ottertrack's north cliffs from the water, grey rock with orange lichen, two cedars on a ledge, water so clear the stones show at the bottom of the frame.

P3.text: Drugstore print, matte. Dawn on Lake One from the island site: an old canvas A-frame tent pitched on a pad of pine needles (the player's own tent), the lake beyond with mist on it.

P4.text: Print. A big walleye on a flat rock, its eye gold in the flash, a jig in its lip; behind it a low reef point with one dead spruce.

P5.text: Print. Duncan Lake from the ridge trail high above it, the lake long and blue in morning light, the far ridges in layers.

P6.text: Print, underexposed: Winchell's cliffs in evening light, ledges with cedars, mostly shadow.

P7.text: Colour print, 1980s colours. A woman of about 40 sitting on a beach rock in a red wool shirt, laughing hard, holding up a blue enamel coffee pot with a chip on the lip.
P7.back: Before the pot went in. — June

P8.text: Colour print. Five men on a big rounded rock at a campsite, beer cans and a coffee pot; four grinning, one at the edge half-turned to the water under a felt hat (Walt).

P9.text: Colour print, glare across half of it. Glassy water and, under it, a pale red-and-cream shape with a row of dots that are rivets.

P10.text: A print that is almost all black. Along the bottom, a ragged treeline; above it, low, a pale smudge of light, a little streaked as if the camera moved.

P11.text: Polaroid. A wooden trapper's sled with ash runners and rusted iron straps, on a broad lunch rock among young jack pine, two old window sashes on its deck.

P12.text: Print. Wolf tracks pressed into wet sand, big ones and small ones crossing, with a canoe paddle laid beside them for size (only the paddle, no person).

cut.1.picture: Dark. A click. The headlamp's white circle opens on the inside of the shelter, then drops to the player's own hands holding the brown book, the cloth pale at the corners.
cut.1.sound: The click; wind in the trees, far off; a mosquito, then not.

cut.2.picture: The cover opens. The inside front cover. The lamp settles on the top corner.

cut.3.picture: The first page, the circle on the first line.
cut.3.text: May 22 — EP 30 — solo, 7 days food, the old tent.
cut.3.sound: A loon, far down the lake.

cut.4.picture: A page turn. The circle finds a line near the top.
cut.4.text: Up 4:50. T 41. Fog sitting on the water like it pays rent.
cut.4.sound: The fly ticks once in a breeze.

cut.5.text: 2 WE 18 and 19 off the reef at dusk, slow jig. Kept the small one. Thanked him. Ate him.

cut.6.picture: A page turn. The circle rests longer here, on a short line with white space around it; the bracketed pencil below is outside the light.
cut.6.text: Two cups out of habit. Poured the second one in the lake.

cut.7.text: COLO pair with 2 chicks on the back. Nobody ever looks as proud as a loon with two.
cut.7.sound: A loon answers the first one, nearer.

cut.8.picture: Several pages turned together, the headers flicking past: `July 21 — EP 30`, `Aug 8 — EP 38 — the boys`, `Sept 13 — EP 1`, `Oct 12 — EP 33`, `May 17 — EP 16`, `June 9 — EP 12`. Then the circle stops.
cut.8.text: Little Sag with the boys. Whiskey brought the good whiskey and the bad jokes.
cut.8.sound: A breath through the nose: the player almost laughing.

cut.9.picture: More pages, faster: dates, rod numbers, site stars, the hand slowly loosening. The circle stops once more.
cut.9.text: Slept in the canoe, off the point, tied to a snag. Old man's foolishness. Slept fine.

cut.10.picture: The riffle runs on through the rest of the book, too fast to read: the ink turns to pencil, the entries get short, a page is only a column of times and winds. It stops on a page that is different. The hand is the same and not the same: leaning, pressed hard, running downhill. The circle shakes very slightly (the player's hand, not the lamp).
cut.10.text: The last page, all seven lines, in full, held.
cut.10.sound: Everything outside goes quiet: the loons stop. The paper is loud.

cut.11.picture: Held. The circle drifts down the page as a reader's eye would and comes to rest on the last line. After 8 seconds the circle drifts once to the hole the pencil made in "11:40", then back.
cut.11.sound: A single far-off sound that could be a truck door or a beaver's tail. It is a beaver's tail.

cut.12.picture: The book closes in the player's hands. The lamp clicks off. Black.

cut.13.picture: Black, still. Then the ordinary sleep transition and the morning.
